title: Jets, bubbles and bursts of light in Taurus
caption: XZ Tauri, HL Tauri and nearby young stars, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: LDN 1551, XZ Tauri · constellation Taurus · about 450 light-years away (source figure)
credit: Image credit: ESA/Hubble and NASAAcknowledgement: Judy Schmidt

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble view takes in XZ Tauri, a system of several stars, along with its neighbour HL Tauri and a number of other young stellar objects close by in the constellation Taurus.

XZ Tauri is inflating a hot bubble of gas that spreads into the space around it. That space is filled with bright clumps that are themselves pouring out strong winds and jets. Young stars often do this. As they grow, they fling material outward in narrow jets and broader winds, which crash into the surrounding gas and make it glow.

Together, these objects light up the region. Hubble recorded it through a red filter and a narrow filter tuned to hydrogen-alpha light, the red glow given off by energised hydrogen, which is especially good at picking out jets and shocked gas. The official caption offers few other details.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.45 x 3.34 arcminutes) and distance (450 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.5 × 0.4 light-years. Its light set out about 450 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using a red filter and a hydrogen-alpha filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: With only red and hydrogen filters, the colours are a mapping rather than what an eye would see, and the faint jets need long exposures to show.
